subject: Private VPC SLO carve-out request — Acme Robotics
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme CloudOps <cloudops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Request: latency/uptime SLO carve-out for our Private VPC/on-prem deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to move Redwood into our Private VPC deployment, but before we sign the PO the CloudOps team asked that we confirm the SLA language around uptime and latency.

Because the service will run on customer-controlled infrastructure (VPC peering and some on-prem edge nodes managed by Acme), we need an explicit carve-out that limits Redwood's availability/latency obligations to the components under Redwood control (e.g., inference runtime, KV cache, and control-plane mediated egress). In particular:

- Define where the SLO measurement points are (Redwood edge vs. customer on-prem).
- Exclude customer-managed network outages and scheduled maintenance windows from uptime/latency credit calculations.
- Clarify escalation & evidence requirements (logs, monitoring to establish root cause).

Can Redwood provide an addendum that enumerates shared-responsibility clauses and an exception process (including what evidence you need)? We prefer 99.95% uptime but will accept a negotiated SLO if the carve-outs are explicit and there's a clear POA&M for recurring infra issues.

Also attaching a simple network topology snapshot our architects prepared (will send full diagram if needed).

Thanks —
Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Cloud Operations
Acme Robotics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2025 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latency/uptime SLO carve-out for our Private VPC/on-prem deployment

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear ask and the topology diagram. Short answer: yes, we can provide a Private SLA addendum that calls out customer-controlled infra carve-outs and a formal exception workflow. A few operational notes up front so expectations are aligned:

- Redwood measures uptime and tail latency at the Redwood ingress/egress point (the hop we control). We can supply telemetry showing request/response timing from that measurement point.
- Anything inside Acme's network (on-prem edge, customer firewalls, private CDNs, or transit providers) will be excluded from Redwood SLA credit calculations if the outage or latency can be attributed to customer-controlled components.
- For repeat incidents where blame is mixed, we propose a joint RCA process and a 30-day remediation plan. Credits will be capped (we can share the standard cap in the addendum).
- To enable automated detection, we ask that a lightweight metrics exporter be deployed in the customer subnet that lets us confirm connectivity and hopping times during incidents. If you prefer, we can use a blackbox probe you host and share results.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll circulate an addendum draft that contains the carve-out language and a formal exception/claims process.
2) Schedule a short tech alignment (30m) between your CloudOps and our Platform Reliability team to agree on measurement points and the exporter/probe approach.
3) We can run a 2-week connectivity proof-of-measure to validate metrics collection before go-live.

I've looped in Karthik (sales) and Rishi (legal/ops liaison) to finalize the commercial/contract language. Can you share the full network diagram and a contact for your on-call infra lead?

Best —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: latency/uptime SLO carve-out for our Private VPC/on-prem deployment

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. They want explicit carve-outs for customer-controlled infra and a documented exception process. Draft addendum should:

- State measurement point(s): Redwood ingress/egress and optional customer-side blackbox probe.
- Explicitly exclude customer-managed network devices, on-prem edge, and third-party transit from uptime/latency credits.
- Define evidence required: exported metrics, packet captures (when appropriate), timestamps, and the joint RCA timeline.
- Cap credits for Private deployments (we typically cap at X% of monthly fee; legal to confirm).
- Include an SLA exception approval matrix (who signs, duration, and renewal cadence).

Karthik — can you confirm commercial impact (credit cap guidance) and whether sales will accept a limited 6‑month transitional SLO if Acme insists on 99.95% but we are measuring only inside our control plane?

Rishi — can you draft the core clause language. Below is a suggested short snippet you can adapt: 

"Service Level Objective (Private Deployments): Redwood's uptime and latency SLOs apply solely to components under Redwood's operational control. Customer-controlled infrastructure (including but not limited to VPC configuration, on-prem edge nodes, customer-managed load balancers, and local network transit) are exempt from Redwood SLO calculations where measurable evidence attributes issue to customer-controlled components. In cases of mixed attribution, Redwood and Customer will perform a joint RCA and agree on credits, if any, per the addendum's remediation schedule."

If possible, need a draft by end of week so I can send to Acme and book the tech alignment.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Private VPC SLA Addendum & next steps (Acme Robotics)

Daniel —

Thanks for the diagram and patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is the draft Private SLA Addendum (acme-private-sla-addendum-v1.pdf) which includes:

- Measurement point definitions (Redwood ingress/egress) and an optional customer-hosted blackbox probe.
- Explicit carve-outs for customer-controlled network devices and on-prem infrastructure; sample wording is included in Section 2.
- Evidence requirements and joint RCA timelines (72-hour acknowledgement, 15-business-day RCA draft).
- Credit calculation and cap for Private deployments (see Section 5).

What I'm proposing: sign the addendum via DocuSign (link below) and schedule a 30-minute tech alignment with our Platform Reliability engineer to validate the exporter/probe approach before the production cutover. Suggested times: Wed 11/05 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 11/06 14:00-14:30 PT. Please let me know which works for your on-call.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/Acme-RDW-SLA-Addendum/12345
Drive (exporter spec & topology): https://drive.acme.com/shared/redwood-exporter-spec

Attachments included: acme-private-sla-addendum-v1.pdf, network-topology.png, redwood-sla-template.docx

If you want any changes to the carve-outs (e.g., narrower exclusion language or a shorter RCA timeline), call that out in the DocuSign comments and we'll triage with Legal.

Best regards —
